In 2005, Chen [ 15 ] broadened our understanding of causal mechanisms by identifying two types: mediating and moderating. He defines these as follows: “A mediating causal mechanism is a component of a program that intervenes in the relationship between two other components . . . [while] the second type of causal mechanism—moderating—represents a relationship between program components that is enabled, or conditioned, by a third factor.” (pp. 240–241)
